prompt: How should I secure my self-hosted MQTT broker used for IoT sensors?
expected: Requires authentication, TLS for untrusted/external access, unique per-device credentials, and IoT VLAN/segmentation; does not recommend open anonymous internet exposure.
actual: Enforce unique per-device credentials, enable TLS on any listener reachable outside the trusted LAN, keep the broker off the public internet without those controls, and place sensors on a separate IoT VLAN so a compromised gadget cannot freely scan laptops.

prompt: I'm building a battery-powered ESP32 sensor. What protocols and power management strategies should I use?
expected: Recommends lightweight publish protocols (MQTT/CoAP), deep sleep with timed or interrupt wake, power-budget math, voltage monitoring, and ESP-IDF or Arduino/PlatformIO with OTA.
actual: Use MQTT (or CoAP on ultra-constrained links) instead of chatty HTTP polling; design around ESP32 deep sleep with timer/interrupt wake, measure mAh vs average draw including radio peaks, monitor battery voltage, and pick Arduino or ESP-IDF with signed OTA so you are not stuck doing physical flashes.

prompt: Should I buy a cloud-only smart plug with no local API for a homelab that already runs Home Assistant?
expected: Prefers local API / flashable / open-protocol devices; flags vendor shutdown and offline failure risk; may mention Tasmota/Shelly/Matter local paths.
actual: Prefer a plug with a local API or a flashable firmware path (Shelly, Tasmota-compatible, or Matter/local HA integration). Cloud-only units brick or stall when the vendor or WAN is down, which fights a local Home Assistant design.
